introduction: Compounds made entirely of just 'Carbon (C) and Hydrogen (H)' are called Hydrocarbons. They are the primary components of petroleum, natural gas, and all fossil fuels.

core_concepts.title: Saturated Hydrocarbons (Alkanes)
core_concepts.description:
Carbon atoms are connected by ONLY 'Single Bonds' (C-C). 
They are generally unreactive. 
General Formula: $C_nH_{2n+2}$ 
Examples: Methane ($CH_4$), Ethane ($C_2H_6$), Propane ($C_3H_8$).

core_concepts.title: Unsaturated Hydrocarbons
core_concepts.description:
Carbon atoms contain at least one 'Double Bond' or 'Triple Bond'. They are highly reactive. 
1. Alkenes: Contain a Double Bond (C=C). Formula: $C_nH_{2n}$ (e.g., Ethene - $C_2H_4$). 
2. Alkynes: Contain a Triple Bond (C≡C). Formula: $C_nH_{2n-2}$ (e.g., Ethyne/Acetylene - $C_2H_2$).

core_concepts.title: Functional Groups
core_concepts.description:
Specific atoms or groups of atoms that replace hydrogen in a hydrocarbon chain and dictate the 'chemical properties' of the compound. 
- $-OH$ : Alcohol (Suffix: -ol). 
- $-CHO$ : Aldehyde (Suffix: -al). 
- $-COOH$ : Carboxylic Acid (Suffix: -oic acid). 
- $-CO-$ : Ketone (Suffix: -one).

core_concepts.title: Isomerism
core_concepts.description:
Compounds that have the 'Same Chemical Formula' but 'Different Structural Arrangements'. 
Example: Butane ($C_4H_{10}$) has two isomers: n-Butane (a straight chain) and Iso-butane (a branched chain).

important_entities.name: Methane ($CH_4$)
important_entities.key_fact: Marsh Gas / Main Component of CNG
important_entities.significance: Methane is the simplest hydrocarbon. It is called 'Marsh Gas' because it is produced in swampy, marshy areas by the decay of plants. It is the primary component of Biogas and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: When you burn Saturated hydrocarbons (Alkanes), they burn with a 'Clean Blue Flame' (like your kitchen gas stove). But Unsaturated hydrocarbons (Alkenes/Alkynes) burn with a 'Yellow Sooty Flame' (lots of black smoke).

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: The Alkane, Alkene, Alkyne Formula Rule
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
Start with the base $C_nH_{2n}$. 
For Alkane: Add 2 ($C_nH_{2n+2}$). 
For Alkene: Add 0 ($C_nH_{2n}$). 
For Alkyne: Subtract 2 ($C_nH_{2n-2}$).

exam_strategy_tips: NDA/CDS Question: 'Which gas is used for the artificial ripening of fruits and for gas welding?' Answer: Ethyne / Acetylene ($C_2H_2$).
